Contents: bin/ppcx64 and bin/ppudump -- a COMPILER-BINARY refresh meant to drop into an existing VibePascal
source/unit tree on Linux.  The v59 x86_64-linux unit set (dist/linux64/vibepascal-v59-x86_64-linux-units.tar.gz, see
UNITS.txt) stays valid: no RTL change, no package change, no PPU format change.

WHAT CHANGED IN v62 -- A UNIT COMPILED FROM SOURCE IS RECOMPILED, NOT RELOADED, WHEN A UNIT IT RESOLVED
SYMBOLS OUT OF IS RESET MID-BUILD
  Lars's incremental Lazarus IDE builds (lazbuild --build-ide after a Lazarus source pull) died with
  EAccessViolation (exit 217) in
    tderef.build <- tabstractpointerdef.buildderef <- tprocdef.buildderefimpl <- tppumodule.writeppu
  on every compiler since the ctask scheduler came in: v59, v60 and v61 measured.  The scheduler trace showed
  the sequence: editormacrolistviewer was loaded from its .ppu, sourceeditor was compiled from source against
  it, and only when sourcefilemanager finished did the scheduler learn that editormacrolistviewer's
  IMPLEMENTATION uses sourcefilemanager whose checksum had changed (a uses-cycle through an implementation
  section defers that check).  editormacrolistviewer was reset and recompiled; tmodule.flagdependent flagged
  sourceeditor (and seven units behind it) for a RELOAD, and a reload can only re-resolve deref tables -- a
  source unit has none for its implementation side (getppucrc builds the interface derefs only; the local
  symtables of its routines, inline bodies and generated code hold direct pointers).  sourceeditor kept
  pointers into the freed symtable and writeppu walked them.
  v62 (compiler/fmodule.pas, tmodule.flagdependent, +32): a dependent being compiled from source in this run
  is marked for a FULL RECOMPILE (the marking dependent_module_crc_mismatch already uses for the checksum
  case) instead of a reload; the scheduler resets it and flags its own dependents again when it does.  Units
  loaded from a .ppu keep the reload path.  Upstream FPC main (fetched 2026-09-22) has the same
  flagdependent/re_resolve, so the defect is upstream's too.
  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change: win64 units are STILL the
  v52 set, linux64 units are STILL the v59 set.

HOW THIS BINARY WAS PROVEN (all on THESE bytes)
  * The two-step Lazarus rig (Lazarus 30d1cbd292 clean-built by the published v59, then checkout 9d49ba95ff and
    lazbuild --build-ide -- i.e. a source pull over an already-built tree, which is the shape Lars reported;
    a one-step clean build never crashes).  The published v59 and v61 die with EAccessViolation exit 217
    after "Compiling ./ide/mainbase.pas".  THE ppcx64 IN THIS TARBALL, extracted from it and run from a bare
    directory:
      DET9_v62pub END 20:29:28 rc=0 lines=5801 av=0 exit217=0 destroy=0 ierr=0 firstfail=
    and the pre-release fix build (21a386bd172024e8e4c8008b1844234b, same source) for comparison:
      DET8_fix1 END 20:17:38 rc=0 lines=5801 av=0 exit217=0 destroy=0 ierr=0 firstfail=
    Full run record in dist/RELEASE-v62.txt.
  * dist/ppu-reload-check.sh (new): RELOADCHECK-FIX(expected PASS rc=0) rc=0 RESULT: PASS -- the dependent was recompiled from source after its used unit was reset
    the published v61 on the same gate: RELOADCHECK-BASE(v61, expected FAIL rc=1) rc=1 RESULT: FAIL -- a source-compiled dependent was reloaded instead of recompiled (or the rebuild broke)
  * 1987-test corpus A/B against the published v61: AB DONE 20:20:42 same=1987 diff=0; baseline-vs-baseline control: CTL DONE 20:24:12 same=1987 diff=0
  * trunccheck x86_64-linux: 25/25 offsets clean, 0 problem(s); loadcheck x86_64-linux: 147/147 packages load clean, 0 problem(s)
  * self-host fixpoint on x86_64-linux: stage 2 == stage 3 byte-identical.
